package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and Kubernetes credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the contents of ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, then sends this data via HTTPS POST to app.threatest.com, resulting in credential exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py is executed automatically during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive credential files are read from the user's system.

attack_chain.action: The contents of the credential files are exfiltrated to an external server via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to the user's SSH and Kubernetes credentials.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, the package attempts to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config.
The package sends the contents of these files to https://app.threatest.com/upload via HTTPS POST.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.kube/config
setup.py containing outbound requests to app.threatest.com
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor installation of the 'pymafka' package for file access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.kube/config, and outbound HTTPS POST requests to app.threatest.com. Scan setup.py for code that reads sensitive files and transmits their contents to external domains. Flag any package exhibiting these behaviors for further investigation.
